subject: Architecture
title: The Ronan Point Tower Collapse
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Ronan Point Tower Collapse usable.

hook.text: In 1968, a gas explosion in a London apartment blew out one wall — and the entire corner of the building fell.

buildup.text: Ronan Point was a 22-story tower built from prefabricated concrete panels bolted together like a house of cards.

discovery.text: Removing one panel triggered 'progressive collapse' — each floor fell onto the one below in a chain reaction.

twist.text: Only four people died because the explosion happened at 5:45 AM — most residents were still asleep on the other side.

climax.text: Building codes worldwide changed. Structures now must resist progressive collapse from any single failure.

punchline.text: One blown-out panel. A 22-story tower came down like dominoes.

quiz.question: What type of failure destroyed Ronan Point?
options: Foundation settlement caused by poor soil analysis
Progressive collapse triggered by one panel's removal
Steel corrosion from exposure to coastal salt air

details.summary: Ronan Point was a 22-story London tower block that partially collapsed in 1968 when a gas explosion blew out a load-bearing wall panel. The failure cascaded floor by floor in a progressive collapse, killing four people and exposing fatal weaknesses in prefabricated concrete panel construction.
details.whyItMatters: Ronan Point changed building codes worldwide. It introduced the concept of progressive collapse prevention — the principle that one local failure should never cause the entire structure to fail like a house of cards.
takeaways: A gas explosion triggered progressive collapse of a 22-story tower
Prefabricated concrete panels lacked adequate structural connections
It forced global building codes to address progressive collapse

faq.question: What is progressive collapse?
faq.answer: When one structural element fails and the load transfers to adjacent elements which also fail, causing a chain reaction. At Ronan Point, losing one wall panel caused the floor above to drop, which knocked out the panel below, cascading all the way down the corner of the building.

faq.question: How did Ronan Point change building design?
faq.answer: Codes now require structural redundancy and alternate load paths — if any single element is removed, remaining structures must carry the redistributed load without collapse. This principle was reinforced after the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing and 2001 World Trade Center attacks.
